data.insight: A* found the optimal fastest route (59 min) expanding 13 nodes, 32% fewer than uniform-cost search (19). Greedy best-first expanded only 9 but its route is 58% worse — it chases straight-line closeness and ignores congestion.
data.heuristic: h(n) = straight-line km to goal ÷ 55 km/h (fastest free-flow speed) — never overestimates, so A* is optimal.

model.method: Finite-horizon MDP solved exactly by backward induction (Bellman optimality)
assumptions: One decision per hour. Trips per hour = usable minutes ÷ (wait + pickup + ride).
Waiting time falls with zone demand on a convex curve (3 + 42·(1 − score/100)² minutes), shared with DemandService.
Trip destinations follow a gravity model: weight ∝ (destination demand + 15) · e^(−km/6). The destination of the last trip is where the driver ends the hour.
Repositioning burns fuel and its travel minutes are lost from the hour.
